reviews.title: Really cool learning tool
reviews.text: Every day one can learn about something new. Today, clowns; yesterday, baby animals; in the past, photography, time travel, space travel, the human digestive system, the tongue. The five games include putting events on a timeline, deciding who’s (or what’s) better at something, slotting things on a sort of mind map, a vocabulary exercise, and the newest one, guessing the date and location from a photo. You may not love every day’s subject, but there will be enough subjects that get you excited. Also, there’s access to the whole past library (or some of it anyway.)

reviews.title: Wish they kept it free.
reviews.text: I love spark, I enjoy having a break from my day to day tasks and feeling like I am being productive and learning. However, I feel like I am constantly being pushed to purchase features. I get it. There is a lot of work that goes into creating and maintaining an app. My favorite part of Spark however was that it felt based around a community, and its free aspect felt like a way to share and connect people to education no matter their circumstances. I’m really disappointed by the bombardment of memberships and plans, and the removal of features that used to be free. I would gladly donate to keep spark free for EVERYONE, instead of having features behind a paywall.

reviews.title: ENDED MY DOOMSCROLLING
reviews.text: I never leave reviews, but I love Spark so much, I just had to. In the past, I used to go straight to YouTube shorts right after I woke up. This would seep into the rest of the day, and I’d find myself navigating to YouTube whenever I had free time. However, Spark keeps their puzzles concise and easy enough to do right after I wake, and I like that it allows me to set up my day with good intentions. After I finish my Spark puzzles (which don’t eat up my morning like doomscrolling can), I’m way more likely to choose brain workout apps or books over mindlessly navigating to social media. Thank you, Spark!
